memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain and
said, 'This is what you are to say to the descendants of Jacob and what you are
to tell the people of Israel: "You yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt, and
how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself."'"
- Ex 19:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before God gives a single command, He reminds them what He has done.

That order matters enormously. Everything in the next chapters, the covenant,
the commandments, the whole law, comes after this sentence. God does not say
"obey Me and then I will rescue you." He says: I already rescued you.

Notice the image. "I carried you on eagles' wings." An eagle does not drag its
young or push them. It carries them. Israel's part in the exodus was to be
carried.

And notice the destination: "and brought you to myself." Not merely out of Egypt,
and not merely to a mountain. To Himself. That was always the point.

This is the pattern the whole Bible follows. Grace comes first, then response.
Paul spends eleven chapters of Romans on what God has done before he writes,
"Therefore, I urge you... in view of God's mercy" (Rom 12:1). The therefore rests
on everything before it.

If your Christian life feels like an exhausting attempt to earn something, this
verse resets the order. You are not carrying yourself. You are being carried, and
you are being carried toward God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you live as though obedience earns God's favour or responds to it?
2. What has God already done for you that you keep forgetting?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You carried me before You ever asked anything of me. Let
my obedience be a response to Your mercy, not an attempt to earn it. Amen.
